name: CA-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Post-redistricting fundamentals strongly favor Democrats (D+7 lean, ~13.5-point fundamentals margin)
Polymarket prices the Democrat at about 97% to win
Mike McGuire has outraised incumbent James Gallagher and enjoys outside support
No public general-election polling, so the forecast rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: The redrawn district's fundamentals point clearly toward Democrats, and prediction markets price the race near-certainly Democratic despite Gallagher's incumbency. McGuire's fundraising edge reinforces the picture, so the forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based margin.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Gallagher running competitively, or a shift in the national House environment, would be the main signal to revisit this rating.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; fundamentals point clearly one way (post-redistricting), so it is treated as safe for that party.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
California's 1st District was redrawn to lean Democratic, and the fundamentals now point clearly that way despite Republican incumbent James Gallagher running for re-election. Democratic state senator Mike McGuire has raised more money than Gallagher and benefits from outside spending, while no outside groups are opposing him. Prediction markets price McGuire's chances at roughly 97 percent.

With no public general-election polling available, the forecast rests on the district's partisan lean, the favorable national environment for Democrats, and McGuire's financial position. Incumbency gives Gallagher a modest offset, but not enough to change the race's direction. The race is rated Safe Democratic, with uncertainty somewhat elevated because direct polling evidence is absent.
